description: Hindlimb proportions of 49 Carnivora and ungulates: MT/F = metatarsal / femur, hind leg = femur + tibia + metatarsal (digits excluded). Donors map body_blockout presets to species.

source.citation: Garland T Jr, Janis CM (1993). Does metatarsal/femur ratio predict maximal running speed in cursorial mammals? Journal of Zoology, London 229: 133-151. Data from Fig. 1 (p. 136).
source.licence_text: Numeric facts transcribed from a published figure; facts are not copyrightable. The paper itself is not redistributed.
source.attribution: Hindlimb data from Garland T Jr & Janis CM (1993), J. Zool. Lond. 229: 133-151, Fig. 1.
source.modification: Derived/modified: the 49 rows of Fig. 1 transcribed and checked against a render of p. 136. Femur, tibia and metatarsal lengths are derived from hind leg length and MT/F assuming tibia = femur; donor bands are the family ranges in the same figure; digit lengths are recalled values (warnings only).
source.caveats: Limb lengths are maximum articular lengths (Scott 1985) of mostly wild-shot museum specimens; hind leg = femur + tibia + metatarsal and excludes the digits. Domestic dog and cat are not in the table.

wolf.note: Domestic dogs are Canis lupus familiaris; the wild wolf is the table's nearest row.

mt_f.src: Garland & Janis 1993, Fig. 1: Panthera leo; band = Felidae range over 4 species

felid.note: Felis catus is not in the table. Felid long-bone lengths scale isometrically and felids keep a crouched posture at every size (Cuff et al. 2016, J. Anat., PMC5341591), so the lion's ratio stands in for the cat; check against domestic-cat skeletons when one is fetched.

horse.note: Pastern = fetlock to coffin joint (P1 + P2); hoof = coffin joint to the toe on the ground (P3).
